properties.description:
`reflow2-mcp --read-only` refuses every write and still answers every read. Delivers `req:the-hosted-surface-is-read-only-so-it-can-ship-before-authentication-exists`.

📌 The near-match offered was `chg:a-read-only-surface-refuses-at-the-write-guard`, which is the EVENT of building this on 2026-08-26. This is the standing CAPABILITY. The event is what happened once; the capability is what the system can do from now on, and it is the thing a requirement is satisfied BY.

⭐ THE ENFORCEMENT POINT IS THE DESIGN. It refuses in `ReflowService::write_lock` — the graph's write guard, which every mutating handler must obtain and no write can avoid. So it covers all 98 write sites that exist and every write added later, including by an author who never heard of the mode.

The alternative was a list of mutating tool names, or a check keyed on the `readOnlyHint` annotation each tool declares. Both are rules maintained BY HAND with nothing checking them — the defect class this project fixed three times on 2026-08-26 (`unallocated_component` and the parking ruling; F-01's replay contract; three detectors not reading `proposed`). Choosing that form here, the same day, would have been remarkable.

⭐ THE COMPILER PROVED THE SWEEP COMPLETE. Making `write_lock` fallible turned all 98 call sites into compile errors until each was updated — no list, no audit, no chance of missing one. It also found a case review would not have: `share()` is a SECOND assembly point, minting a service per CLIENT SESSION (`req:sessions-share-a-graph`), and read-only had to be INHERITED there. Reset, the mode would have held for the process and evaporated for every actual client — read-only in name only, testing green at the process level.

⚠️ WHAT IT DELIVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. **INTEGRITY** is answered outright: no write means nothing to attribute, so the caller-supplied `contributor_id` — an unverified claim over a network — is never accepted. **CONFIDENTIALITY** is NOT eliminated, only RELOCATED to the network, which is what binding to a tailnet is for. This is not authentication and must not be read as making authentication unnecessary; it is what lets a reachable surface ship BEFORE authentication exists.

🛑 OFF BY DEFAULT. `read_only: false` in `wrap_at`, the single assembly point; the flag appears in no shipped config. `a_normal_service_still_writes` pins that an ordinary service is writable and passed both before and after the refusal landed.

The refusal is LOUD, naming the mode and the reason, so a caller can tell "this server refuses writes" from "this write was wrong" — the same call `dec:stateless-seat-handle` makes about a missing seat: a loud refusal beats a quiet wrong answer.
properties.name: A server can refuse every write, at the one point a write cannot avoid
